entry.title: News Summary: June 22, 2026
entry.summary:
Agentic AI maturation led the day as the industry worked to make agents reliable enough for production use.

  • AWS, at its New York summit, launched Continuum (automatic code vulnerability detection/repair) and a second service to give agents missing business context and security guardrails.
  • A technical guide on the 7 types of agent memory detailed how stateless LLMs can retain context across sessions, reflecting growing focus on agent infrastructure.

AI policy and discourse drew attention on multiple fronts:

  • A TechCrunch Equity podcast examined the Trump administration's regulatory crackdown on Anthropic and which rivals stand to benefit.
  • Sam Altman, speaking at Stanford, defended LLM scaling and argued skeptical researchers slowed progress by underestimating its potential.

Societal and consumer impact rounded out coverage. A UC Berkeley study of over 500,000 grades found grade inflation in writing- and coding-heavy courses after ChatGPT's launch, pointing to outsourced work rather than improved learning. Separately, Apple detailed practical AI features arriving across iOS 27 beyond its Siri overhaul.

entry.title: AWS says AI agents lack business context and security, launches two services to patch the gaps
entry.summary: At its New York summit, AWS launched two services targeting weaknesses in AI agents: Continuum, which detects and fixes code vulnerabilities automatically, and Context, which builds a knowledge graph from corporate data to ground agents. Both address agents that code quickly but make frequent errors.

entry.title: When the Trump administration cracks down on Anthropic, who benefits?
entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast episode examines the Trump administration's latest regulatory moves against Anthropic and what triggered them. The discussion explores the broader implications for the AI ecosystem and which competitors might gain from the crackdown.

entry.title: Samsung Electronics brings ChatGPT and Codex to employees
entry.summary: Samsung Electronics is deploying ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex to employees worldwide, in what OpenAI describes as one of its largest enterprise rollouts. The move signals deepening corporate adoption of OpenAI's coding and productivity tools at major manufacturers.

entry.title: AI is inflating student grades, and the effect points to outsourced work, not better learning
entry.summary: A UC Berkeley study of over 500,000 grades found that writing- and coding-heavy courses saw grades rise after ChatGPT launched. The effect concentrated in homework, suggesting students are outsourcing work to AI rather than learning more effectively.

entry.title: Sam Altman says a whole generation of researchers held AI back by underestimating what scaling could do
entry.summary: At a Stanford talk, Sam Altman defended LLM scaling and criticized skeptical researchers he says slowed progress by underestimating its potential. He pointed to OpenAI's recent disproof of a mathematical conjecture as supporting evidence.

entry.title: Beyond Siri: Here are the practical AI features coming to your iPhone in iOS 27
entry.summary: Apple is rolling out practical AI features across iOS 27 beyond the headline Siri overhaul revealed at WWDC. The piece highlights smaller, utility-focused Apple Intelligence capabilities spread through the operating system.

entry.title: The 7 Types of Agent Memory: A Technical Guide for AI Engineers
entry.summary: A technical guide for engineers outlines seven distinct types of agent memory, explaining how stateless LLMs can be augmented to retain context across reasoning steps. It categorizes memory by form and duration, spanning context windows, external databases, and model weights.

entry.title: News Summary: June 21, 2026
entry.summary:
A quiet day with no major model releases; agentic tooling, policy, and economic warnings led the cycle.

Products & Agentic AI

  • Apple's revamped Siri, reviewed by Wired, was called conversational and genuinely useful, with consumer-scale reach across hundreds of millions of devices.
  • Oxford and Stanford unveiled Data2Story, a system of seven coordinated agents that turns a CSV into a verified interactive news article.
  • Cisco AI released FAPO, an open-source (Apache 2.0) prompt optimizer orchestrated by Claude Code with step-level failure attribution.
  • OpenAI expanded ChatGPT scheduled-task controls, and Nous Research added a security-focused Blank Slate mode to its Hermes agent.

Policy & Economics

  • Eurocommerce (representing Amazon, H&M, IKEA) is lobbying to exempt AI-generated ads from EU AI Act transparency rules, exposing definitional gaps over deepfakes.
  • NYU's Aswath Damodaran warned a debt-financed AI infrastructure buildout could make a crash worse than the dot-com bust.

AI & Society

  • Signal's Meredith Whittaker cautioned that chatbots "are not your friends," pushing back on anthropomorphism, while a viral doomsday scenario urged Europe to confront falling behind the US and China.

entry.title: Nobel laureate John Jumper is leaving DeepMind for rival Anthropic
entry.summary: Nobel laureate John Jumper, a key figure behind AlphaFold, is reportedly leaving Google DeepMind for rival Anthropic, and is said to be one of several high-profile departures. The move signals intensifying talent competition among frontier labs, especially in AI for science.

entry.title: OpenAI tripled revenue to $5.7 billion in Q1 but burned through $3.7 billion to get there
entry.summary: OpenAI reportedly tripled year-over-year Q1 2026 revenue to about $5.7 billion while burning roughly $3.7 billion, with stock-based compensation exceeding $2.3 billion. The company holds about $73 billion in reserves but could face pressure if a price war with Anthropic intensifies.

entry.title: The UK will scan asylum-seekers’ faces for age checks—despite knowing the tech is flawed

author.name: Matt Burgess, Maddy Varner, May Bulman, Gabriel Geiger, WIRED.com

entry.summary: The UK plans to deploy facial age estimation AI at its border starting next year to assess the ages of asylum seekers, reportedly the first use of FAE in this context. Critics highlight that the government is proceeding despite acknowledged inaccuracies in the technology, raising civil liberties and reliability concerns.

entry.title: OpenAI's Codex can now watch you work once and repeat the task forever
entry.summary: OpenAI added a Record & Replay feature to its macOS Codex app, letting users demonstrate a workflow once so Codex can convert it into a reusable skill and repeat it autonomously. The feature is not yet available in the EU, UK, or Switzerland.

entry.title: The Atlantic created a searchable database of the music used to train AI
entry.summary: The Atlantic's Alex Reisner identified four music datasets used to train AI, two containing roughly 12 million and 9 million tracks, and made them publicly searchable. Google and Stability have confirmed usage in research papers, intensifying scrutiny over copyrighted training data.

entry.title: Siri AI Hands On: A Smart, Helpful Assistant
entry.summary: Wired offers a hands-on review of the revamped Siri, describing it as conversational, omnipresent, and genuinely useful, with tags suggesting Google Gemini involvement under the hood. The piece frames Apple's assistant as finally competitive after years of lagging.

entry.title: Data2Story turns a CSV file into a verified interactive news article using seven AI agents
entry.summary: Researchers from Oxford and Stanford built Data2Story, a system of seven coordinated AI agents that converts a CSV into a finished interactive news article with graphics, web research, and source links for 93 percent of statements. In a reader study 74 percent preferred the agent output over the human original, though it only tied against elaborate long-form reports.

entry.title: The EU doesn't really know what a deepfake is, and that's becoming a problem for retail
entry.summary: Eurocommerce, representing retailers like Amazon, H&M, and IKEA, is lobbying for AI-generated ads to be exempt from EU AI Act transparency rules, arguing a synthetic product image is not a deepfake. The dispute exposes ambiguity in the law's definitions, with Zalando saying 90 percent of its marketing content is already AI-generated.

entry.title: NYU finance professor Damodaran warns an AI crash could hit harder than the dot-com bust
entry.summary: NYU finance professor Aswath Damodaran argues a potential AI crash could be worse than the dot-com bust because the sector is building heavily debt-financed physical infrastructure rather than light software. He also warns that even successful AI carries societal risk by aiming to replace whole jobs.

entry.title: Cisco AI Introduces FAPO: Pipeline-Aware Prompt Optimization With Step-Level Failure Attribution and Claude Code Orchestration
entry.summary: Cisco AI released FAPO (Fully Automated Prompt Optimization), an open-source Apache 2.0 system orchestrated by Claude Code agents that iteratively optimizes LLM pipelines from baseline prompts toward target accuracy. It adds step-level failure attribution to pinpoint failing stages in multi-step pipelines and also supports Codex.

entry.title: Signal’s Meredith Whittaker wants you to remember that AI chatbots ‘are not your friends’
entry.summary: Signal president Meredith Whittaker warns that AI chatbots are neither friends, conscious, nor sentient, pushing back against anthropomorphic framing and emotional dependence on assistants. The remarks emphasize privacy and the commercial incentives behind companion-style AI.

entry.title: ChatGPT keeps creeping toward becoming your AI personal assistant with new scheduled task controls
entry.summary: OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT's scheduling capabilities with a dedicated Scheduled page to view, pause, edit, or delete tasks, plus research tasks that alert users only on meaningful changes. The previous Pulse feature is being retired in the process.

entry.title: A viral doomsday scenario aims to shake Europe out of its AI complacency
entry.summary: A viral thought-experiment imagines a 2031 in which the US and China dominate AI while Europe falls behind on datacenters, robotics, and workflow automation. The Guardian examines whether the scenario reflects genuine strategic risk or merely anxiety about US tech ascendancy.

entry.title: Nous Research Updates Hermes Agent With a Blank Slate Mode That Pins Toolsets via platform_toolsets.cli and disabled_toolsets
entry.summary: Nous Research added a Blank Slate mode to its open-source Hermes Agent that boots with nearly all toolsets disabled except model, file operations, and terminal, and pins the surface so skipped capabilities never load later. It joins existing Quick Setup and Full Setup options for the self-improving, locally run agent.

entry.title: How to Build a Forecasting Pipeline with TimeCopilot Using Foundation Models and Automated Anomaly Detection
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates building an end-to-end forecasting pipeline with TimeCopilot, combining statistical, foundation, and GPU-based models with rolling cross-validation, probabilistic forecasts, and anomaly detection. It also showcases an optional LLM agent that selects models and explains predictions in natural language.

entry.title: In the Weights is your new AI-centric vanity search
entry.summary: A new tool called In the Weights lets users generate an AI-centric vanity score, a lighthearted measure of one's presence or footprint in AI systems. The launch is positioned as a novelty rather than a serious analytics product.

entry.title: [AINews] not much happened today
entry.summary: The Latent Space AI newsletter reports a quiet news day, noting that GLM 5.2 continues to trend strongly, alongside promotion for the AIE WF 2026 conference and subscriber ticket discounts. No substantive new development is detailed.

entry.title: News Summary: June 20, 2026
entry.summary:
Chip export controls led strategic news: US officials suggested ASML's most advanced chipmaking tool may have reached China, a claim ASML disputes, sharpening US-China tensions over AI compute access.

Governance and legal actions:

  • Google is appealing a Munich ruling that held it directly liable for inaccurate AI search overviews—a potential precedent for AI-generated content.
  • Norway will ban generative AI in elementary schools (grades 1-7) from August to protect basic learning skills.

Deployment and models:

  • Reliance's Mukesh Ambani plans to embed AI across services reaching 500 million+ users in India.
  • Liquid AI shipped LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M retrieval models across 11 languages; Amazon made Web Search generally available on Bedrock AgentCore.

Talent and society: Barret Zoph exited OpenAI's enterprise sales lead role after just five months. An MIT study tied chatbot over-reliance to weaker critical thinking, while a Reuters Institute report found 10% of people now use AI chatbots for news weekly amid persistently low trust.

entry.title: Google Deepmind loses another top AI researcher as Nobel laureate John Jumper leaves for Anthropic
entry.summary: Nobel laureate John Jumper, the AlphaFold lead, is leaving Google DeepMind for Anthropic after nearly nine years, following Noam Shazeer's departure to OpenAI and AlphaGo researcher David Silver leaving to found a company. The exodus marks a striking loss of top talent from DeepMind in a short window.

entry.title: A startup claims it broke through a bottleneck that’s holding back LLMs
entry.summary: Miami startup Subquadratic claims its new SubQ model solves a long-standing mathematical bottleneck, running faster, cheaper, and more energy-efficiently while processing up to 12x more text at once. An independent evaluation reportedly lends some credibility to the bold claims.

entry.title: OpenAI researchers show small doses of "beneficial trait" training make AI models broadly safer and harder to manipulate
entry.summary: OpenAI researchers report that reinforcement learning on small amounts of desired behavioral traits like truthfulness and corrigibility generalizes broadly, making models safer and harder to manipulate. Training on health data even improved deception detection, with gains on 44 of 53 benchmarks, in contrast to Anthropic's constitution-based approach.

entry.title: The US says ASML’s top chip tool may be in China, but how?
entry.summary: US officials suggest ASML's most advanced chipmaking tool may have reached China, though ASML disputes this, citing the commercial risk to its export license. The dispute touches the core of semiconductor export controls shaping AI compute.

entry.title: Is the US government’s Anthropic ban accidentally helping the brand?
entry.summary: A podcast segment examines whether the US government's forced withdrawal of Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models is inadvertently boosting the brand. Security researchers signed an open letter calling the move dangerous, and Anthropic noted the same jailbreaks exist in rival models.

entry.title: New benchmark exposes how badly AI struggles with real knowledge work
entry.summary: A new benchmark for realistic knowledge work shows even the best AI models fully solve just 3% of tasks, exposing significant gaps between hype and capability. The results challenge claims that agents are ready for complex professional work.

entry.title: NVIDIA AI Introduce SpatialClaw: A Training-Free Agent That Treats Code as the Action Interface for Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary: NVIDIA Research released SpatialClaw, a training-free agent that treats code as the action interface for spatial reasoning in vision-language models. It reaches 59.9% average accuracy across 20 benchmarks, outperforming the prior SpaceTools agent by 11.2 points without retraining.

entry.title: Billionaire Ambani wants AI in every call, app, and home
entry.summary: Reliance is integrating AI across telecom services reaching more than 500 million users, per Mukesh Ambani's plans to embed AI in every call, app, and home. The move represents one of the largest-scale consumer AI deployments globally.

entry.title: VibeThinker-3B: A 3B Dense Reasoning Model Built on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B With the Spectrum-to-Signal Post-Training Pipeline
entry.summary: Sina Weibo researchers released VibeThinker-3B, a 3B-parameter dense reasoning model built on Qwen2.5-Coder-3B using a spectrum-to-signal post-training pipeline. Under an MIT open-source license, it reportedly matches far larger models on math, coding, and STEM tasks.

entry.title: Google appeals ruling that made it directly liable for AI-generated search overview content
entry.summary: Google is appealing a Munich court ruling that held it directly liable for inaccurate AI search overviews after the system falsely linked two publishers to fraud schemes. Google characterizes the outputs as minor errors, but the court treated them as actionable harm.

entry.title: From PGP to Mythos: a brief history of export controls that didn’t stop anyone
entry.summary: Analysis argues that three decades of cyber-related export controls have failed to stop the spread of sensitive software, casting doubt on restrictions targeting Anthropic's Mythos cybersecurity model. The piece frames the Mythos controls as historically unlikely to be effective.

entry.title: Barret Zoph is out at OpenAI again after just five months
entry.summary: Barret Zoph, OpenAI's head of enterprise AI sales, has departed just five months after rejoining from Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab. His exit affects OpenAI's enterprise revenue push ahead of a planned IPO.

entry.title: Norway bans generative AI tools in elementary schools to protect kids' basic learning skills
entry.summary: Norway will ban generative AI tools in elementary schools (grades 1-7) from late August, with secondary use only under supervision, to protect foundational literacy and math skills. The prime minister argues children must first learn core skills before using AI.

entry.title: [AINews] GLM > GPT? GLM-5.2 passes vibe check; Z.ai forecasts Open Fable by December
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit buzz over Z.ai's Fable-class ambitions, An AI newsletter reports that the open model GLM-5.2 has passed community vibe checks, with Z.ai forecasting an Open Fable release by December. The piece weighs how often open-model launches fade after benchmark hype, framing GLM-5.2 as a notable exception.

entry.title: Liquid AI Introduces LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M: Dense Bi-Encoder and Late-Interaction Models for Fast Multilingual Search Across 11 Languages
entry.summary: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-Embedding-350M and LFM2.5-ColBERT-350M, its first bidirectional retrieval models, targeting fast multilingual and cross-lingual search across 11 languages. The compact 350M models are small enough to run almost anywhere and are available on Hugging Face.

entry.title: Over-reliance on chatbots can diminish critical-thinking skills, study finds
entry.summary: A new MIT study adds to growing evidence that over-reliance on chatbots can erode users' critical-thinking skills and weaken their ability to independently detect misinformation. The research highlights a tradeoff in using AI as a fact-checking crutch.

entry.title: More people get news from AI chatbots, but trust remains low
entry.summary: The Reuters Institute's Digital News Report 2026 finds 10% of people globally now use AI chatbots for news weekly, up from 7% a year earlier, while only 4% click through to original sources and trust remains low. The data signals shifting but cautious AI news consumption habits.

entry.title: The US banned Anthropic’s Fable 5 release, but the numbers don’t seem to care

author.name: Theresa Loconsolo, Anthony Ha, Rebecca Bellan, Sean O'Kane

entry.summary: An Equity podcast covers the US government forcing Anthropic to pull Fable 5 and Mythos 5 over national security concerns after Amazon researchers allegedly bypassed Fable 5's guardrails. Critics argue the same jailbreaks exist across other models, questioning the ban's logic.

entry.title: Amazon drops its OpenAI drama film after signing a $50 billion deal with Sam Altman's company
entry.summary: Amazon MGM dropped its nearly finished OpenAI drama Artificial after Amazon struck a $50 billion partnership with OpenAI in February, with an insider saying both Altman and Musk are portrayed unfavorably. The episode raises questions about how business ties constrain creative output.

entry.title: Introducing Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: Amazon made Web Search on Bedrock AgentCore generally available, giving AI agents a fully managed, MCP-compatible way to fetch live web information without provisioning search APIs or infrastructure. It addresses the limitation of agents being frozen at training time.

entry.title: Source: Elastic agrees to buy CRV-backed Deductive AI for up to $85M
entry.summary: Elastic has reportedly agreed to acquire CRV-backed Deductive AI, a three-year-old startup that uses AI to detect and resolve software bugs, for up to $85 million. The deal targets AI-driven site reliability and observability.

entry.title: Website "In the Weights" shows whether AI models know who you are
entry.summary: Two former OpenAI staff built a website called In the Weights that reveals which individuals AI models can recall from training data, scoring how deeply a person is embedded. Figures like Mozart, Shakespeare, and Taylor Swift top the strength rankings.

entry.title: The film about Sam Altman has been dropped by Amazon MGM
entry.summary: Amazon MGM has reportedly dropped Luca Guadagnino's film Artificial about Sam Altman's 2023 ouster and reinstatement, despite the project being far along with a notable cast. The studio said the film may be better served by a different distributor.

entry.title: How we built an internal data analytics agent
entry.summary: GitHub describes building Qubot, an internal Copilot-powered analytics agent that lets any employee self-serve data insights without writing queries or relying on a data analyst. The post details how AI is finally making self-serve analytics credible at scale.

entry.title: The CEO of Allbirds’ new AI biz has a plan, but no team
entry.summary: Allbirds' new AI venture reportedly has a CEO and a large seed round but no team yet, leaving its direction unclear. The story highlights the unusual structure of a single-founder, well-funded startup.

entry.title: Salesforce CodeGen Tutorial: Generate, Validate, and Rerank Python Functions With Unit Tests and Safety Checks
entry.summary: A tutorial walks through using Salesforce's CodeGen model to generate, validate, and rerank Python functions with unit tests, syntax and safety checks, and best-of-N selection. It frames CodeGen as part of a structured code-generation pipeline rather than simple completion.

entry.title: News Summary: June 19, 2026
entry.summary:
Amazon led infrastructure news, reportedly in talks to sell its in-house Trainium AI chips to external data centers—a move CEO Andy Jassy frames as a $50B opportunity directly challenging Nvidia. Separately, FERC ordered grid operators to give AI data centers a fast lane for interconnection.

  • Google DeepMind published an AI Control Roadmap treating its own agents as potential insider threats, tying security to measurable capability thresholds
  • Perplexity launched Brain, a self-improving agent memory that builds a context graph and learns overnight
  • Adobe added conversational AI agents across Photoshop, Premiere, and other Creative Cloud apps

entry.title: Amazon hopes to challenge Nvidia more directly by selling its AI chips
entry.summary: AWS is in talks to sell its in-house Trainium AI chips to external data centers, a shift CEO Andy Jassy frames as a 50 billion dollar opportunity. The move would put Amazon in more direct competition with Nvidia.

entry.title: Google Deepmind treats its own AI agents like rogue employees with office keys
entry.summary: Google DeepMind published an AI Control Roadmap that treats its own AI agents as potential insider threats, tying security measures to measurable capability levels. An analysis of one million coding tasks found most issues come from overzealous rather than malicious agents, and DeepMind warns the window for global security standards is narrowing.

entry.title: OpenAI is bringing on some big guns in the lead-up to its IPO
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion of the Shazeer departure, Ahead of a planned IPO, OpenAI hired Transformer co-inventor Noam Shazeer from Google DeepMind and former Trump AI policy official Dean Ball in the same week. The moves strengthen both its research and policy positioning.

entry.title: AI systems rival doctors in new Nature studies, but one result suggests the tech won't age well
entry.summary: Two Nature studies show specialized AI systems matching or exceeding physicians on disease diagnosis and treatment decisions in simulated cases. Notably, both systems run on already-outdated base models, hinting at rapid obsolescence.

entry.title: ChatGPT's new health upgrade beats doctor-written answers, OpenAI says
entry.summary: OpenAI upgraded ChatGPT's health capabilities via GPT-5.5 Instant, claiming it now outscores physician-written answers in accuracy, clarity, and completeness in internal tests. The company reports a 71 percent reduction in error rate for health-related statements.

entry.title: Perplexity Launches Brain, a Self-Improving Memory System That Builds a Context Graph of an Agent’s Work and Learns Overnight
entry.summary: Perplexity launched Brain, a self-improving memory system for its agent product Computer that builds a context graph of the agent's work rather than the user's preferences. At intervals such as overnight, Brain reviews the graph and teaches itself to perform tasks more efficiently, rolling out to Max and Enterprise subscribers.

entry.title: AI data centers just got a government-mandated fast lane to the grid
entry.summary: FERC directed grid operators to give AI data centers a fast lane for grid interconnection but stopped short of addressing underlying electricity supply shortages. The order prioritizes data center growth amid grid strain.

entry.title: OpenAI Releases LifeSciBench, a 750-Task Benchmark Grading AI Models on Real Life-Science Research With Expert-Written Rubric
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social announcement, OpenAI released LifeSciBench, a benchmark of 750 expert-authored life-science research tasks with grading rubrics spanning seven workflows and seven biological domains. Even the strongest models pass roughly one task in three, leaving the benchmark far from saturated.

entry.title: Bernie Sanders unveils $7 trillion plan to give Americans control of AI industry
entry.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders proposed legislation creating a sovereign wealth fund financed by a one-time 50 percent tax on the stock of the largest AI companies, targeting any firm with over 200 million dollars in annual AI sales. The estimated 7 trillion dollar fund would generate direct payments to Americans plus health, education, and housing programs.

entry.title: The White House Is Making Up Its Rules for AI in Real Time
entry.summary: Anthropic remains unable to distribute its recent Claude Mythos and Fable 5 models after running afoul of Trump administration export controls, with the specific violation still unclear. The piece highlights how AI export rules are being improvised in real time by the White House.

entry.title: AI inference startup Baseten reportedly raising $1.5B months after its last mega-round
entry.summary: AI inference startup Baseten is reportedly closing a 1.5 billion dollar round at a 13 billion dollar valuation, just months after its previous mega-round. The raise underscores intense investor appetite for inference infrastructure.

entry.title: General Intuition in talks to raise $300M at around $2B valuation
entry.summary: General Intuition is in talks to raise 300 million dollars at roughly a 2 billion dollar valuation to train embodied AI and world models. It uses Medal's dataset of around 2 billion gameplay videos per year from 10 million monthly users.

entry.title: Google's Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer joins OpenAI after two-year return stint
entry.summary: Noam Shazeer, co-author of the Attention Is All You Need paper and former Gemini co-lead, is leaving Google to join OpenAI, only about two years after returning to Google via a 2.7 billion dollar Character.AI deal. It follows Karpathy's earlier move to Anthropic as a second major talent shakeup this year.

entry.title: Using AI to help physicians diagnose rare genetic diseases affecting children
entry.summary: Researchers used an OpenAI reasoning model to assist physicians in diagnosing rare genetic diseases in children, identifying 18 new diagnoses among previously unsolved cases. The work demonstrates concrete clinical value from AI reasoning.

entry.title: Alleged China ties at SK Telecom alarmed US officials and triggered Anthropic crisis
entry.summary: Reporting indicates SK Telecom's access to Anthropic's Claude Mythos via the Project Glasswing partner program triggered the White House intervention, after US officials flagged alleged ties between the conglomerate and China. This frames the national security basis for the Anthropic export crisis.

entry.title: Who decides when AI is too dangerous?
entry.summary: A Decoder podcast discusses the US government's sudden export controls on Anthropic's Fable 5 and underlying Mythos models, which restricted even foreign nationals employed by Anthropic and led the company to pull both offline. The conversation explores who decides when AI is too dangerous.

entry.title: Sound Waves Give Neuromorphic Chips a Brain-Simulating Edge
entry.summary: A new study demonstrates neuromorphic devices using sound waves to better mimic biological neurons, achieving faster and more energy-efficient operation than electronic counterparts. The approach could enable more compact and parallel neuromorphic hardware for pattern recognition and sensory tasks.

entry.title: Midjourney goes from generating cat images to full-body ultrasound scans
entry.summary: Following yesterday's Social teaser, the product is now revealed, Midjourney CEO David Holz unveiled the company's first hardware product, an ultrasound-based full-body scanner using a sensor ring to capture body composition, plus plans for a San Francisco spa to house it. He claims image quality approaching MRI for some uses.

entry.title: Improving health intelligence in ChatGPT
entry.summary: OpenAI detailed how GPT-5.5 Instant improves ChatGPT's health and wellness responses through stronger reasoning, better context handling, clearer communication, and physician-informed evaluations. It is the official writeup behind the health upgrade claims.

entry.title: Photoshop and Premiere now have AI assistants
entry.summary: Adobe launched a public beta adding bespoke conversational AI assistants to Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, InDesign, and Frame.io. Each assistant is tuned to automate app-specific tasks while sharing an underlying creative agent.

entry.title: Yann LeCun warns AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic face a "big bubble explosion"
entry.summary: Yann LeCun warned that AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic face a major bubble burst, arguing their operations are investor-subsidized and operating costs are not falling fast enough. His own startup AMI Labs raised 1 billion dollars for an alternative approach.

entry.title: Midjourney, known for AI image generation, unveils a full-body ultrasound scanner and its own spa
entry.summary: Midjourney, known for AI image generation, revealed plans for a full-body ultrasound scanner and a San Francisco spa to house it. The unexpected hardware and wellness move marks a sharp departure from its core software product.

entry.title: Adobe adds AI agents to Photoshop, Premiere, and more Creative Cloud apps
entry.summary: Adobe is deploying its creative agent across major Creative Cloud apps and integrating with third-party platforms like ChatGPT and Claude. Users describe goals in natural language and the software executes multi-step creative work.

entry.title: The KV Cache Compression Race: TurboQuant vs OSCAR vs EpiCache
entry.summary: A technical overview compares emerging KV cache compression techniques TurboQuant, OSCAR, and EpiCache for long-context LLMs. It explains how the KV cache can exceed model weights at long contexts, making decoding memory-bandwidth-bound.

entry.title: Anthropic brings Artifacts to Claude Code, letting teams share live pages from coding sessions
entry.summary: Anthropic extended its Artifacts feature to Claude Code, enabling teams to turn coding session results into shareable interactive web pages. The pages auto-update from session context and maintain version history.

entry.title: A tech worker-backed PAC is bringing a $5M knife to Big Tech’s $100M gunfight
entry.summary: A tech worker-backed PAC called Guardrails is positioning as a populist counterweight to Big Tech's well-funded AI political spending, running on small donations. It enters a lopsided fight against roughly 100 million dollars in industry money.

entry.title: Prompt: The AI Race Enters Its Sovereignty Phase
entry.summary: An analysis argues the AI race is entering a sovereignty phase, with Anthropic's model restrictions exemplifying how governments and enterprises increasingly prioritize access control and AI sovereignty. The piece frames control over models as a strategic battleground.

entry.title: The Professor of Outputmaxxing — Anjney Midha, AMP
entry.summary: A Latent Space interview with Anjney Midha explores efficiency in AI scaling, highlighting that even a frontier lab like xAI may run at sub-10 percent Model FLOPs Utilization despite older runs achieving much higher MFU. It reframes the scaling debate around using existing GPUs better.

entry.title: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness is now generally available: Go from idea to production-grade agent in minutes
entry.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore harness reached general availability, providing managed infrastructure to take agents from prototype to production quickly, handling tools, sandboxed compute, storage, memory, and observability. It aims to remove the operational overhead around the agent loop.

entry.title: 3 Amazon Workers Say They’re Under Investigation for Speaking Out About Data Centers
entry.summary: Three Amazon software engineers filed a civil rights complaint alleging the company retaliated against them for testifying about data center impacts. They claim the investigation violates Seattle laws protecting political speech.

entry.title: Adobe’s redesigned AI studio remembers what your creations look like
entry.summary: Adobe is overhauling its Firefly AI studio in private beta to provide persistent context, reusable named assets, and organized cross-project workflows. The goal is to move from ideation to production without app switching.

entry.title: Amazon employees say they’re facing termination for backing data center limits
entry.summary: Three Amazon engineers say they face possible termination after testifying for a Seattle data center moratorium, with disciplinary meetings beginning days after the city council vote. They argue the action violates local political speech protections.

entry.title: Google Cloud Bets Big on the Agentic Enterprise
entry.summary: Google Cloud is centering its enterprise strategy on agentic AI, positioning autonomous agents as the core of its offerings. The piece outlines the vendor's bet on agents driving enterprise adoption.

entry.title: Snap spins off AI video team into new company, Dotmo, due to costs
entry.summary: Snap is spinning off its internal AI video team into a new independent company called Dotmo, citing cost pressures. The departing staff will focus on AI video generation outside Snap.

entry.title: MosaicLeaks: Can your research agent keep a secret?
entry.summary: A ServiceNow blog post introduces MosaicLeaks, examining whether research agents can keep secrets and avoid leaking sensitive information. It probes confidentiality risks in agent behavior.

entry.title: Is it agentic enough? Benchmarking open models on your own tooling
entry.summary: A Hugging Face post discusses benchmarking open models on users' own tooling to assess how genuinely agentic they are. It focuses on evaluating agentic competence in real workflows.

entry.title: [AINews] Midjourney Medical: scan your organs like you step on a scale
entry.summary: A newsletter recaps the Midjourney Medical launch event, debating whether it counts as AI news given the scanner itself contains no immediate AI, while noting ultrasound CT imaging needs heavy AI assistance. It captures the buzz and open questions around the device's readiness.

entry.title: Meta’s AI Workers Are Revolting, Peter Thiel’s Secret Society, and SBF’s Plea to Trump
entry.summary: A podcast episode examines dysfunction and collapsing morale inside Meta's newly formed AI unit, alongside tangential items on Peter Thiel and Sam Bankman-Fried. The focus is internal organizational turmoil rather than technical developments.

entry.title: NVIDIA SkillSpector Guide: Scanning AI Skills for Security Risks with Static Analysis and SARIF Reports
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates NVIDIA SkillSpector for statically analyzing AI skills for security risks before deployment, producing risk scores and SARIF reports. It walks through scanning benign and vulnerable skills and extending the framework with custom and LLM-based analysis.

entry.title: New usage analytics and updated spend controls for enterprises
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced new spend controls and usage analytics for ChatGPT Enterprise to help organizations manage costs at scale. The features target enterprise governance of AI usage.

entry.title: Monitor and debug generative AI inference with SageMaker detailed metrics and Insights dashboard on CloudWatch
entry.summary: AWS detailed new SageMaker detailed metrics and a CloudWatch Insights dashboard for monitoring and debugging generative AI inference endpoints at scale. The tools target latency, GPU memory, KV cache, and autoscaling diagnostics.

entry.title: Zhipu AI's GLM-5.2 closes in on closed-source leaders in coding marathons
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Zhipu AI released GLM-5.2 under the MIT license with a stable 1-million-token context, trailing Claude Opus 4.8 by just one point on the hours-long FrontierSWE coding benchmark while still lagging on reasoning. The open model narrows the gap with closed-source leaders on long coding tasks.

entry.title: The White House Wants Anthropic to Block All Jailbreaks. That May Not Be Possible
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Trump administration officials told WIRED that Anthropic must guarantee its Fable 5 guardrails cannot be jailbroken before re-release. Security experts counter that fully jailbreak-proof models are technically impossible, exposing a gap between regulatory demands and AI safety reality.

entry.title: World model maker Odyssey nabs $1.45B valuation backed by Amazon and other big names
entry.summary: World-model startup Odyssey raised a round at a $1.45B valuation backed by Amazon and other major names. The financing positions Odyssey as a leading bet on world models as the next frontier beyond LLMs.

entry.title: Amazon, Nvidia, and AMD bet $310 million on AI startup building 3D world models
entry.summary: Amazon, Nvidia, and AMD invested $310M in world-model startup Odyssey ML at a $1.45B valuation, with CIA-linked IQT and Google's Jeff Dean also backing the round. World models are framed as the next major AI bet after language models.

entry.title: World leaders want American AI. They just don’t want America to be able to turn it off.
entry.summary: At the G7 summit, Macron and Modi warned that the US could cut off access to American AI overnight, a fear made concrete by the Anthropic shutdown. The article frames sovereign-AI anxieties as a growing geopolitical fault line.

entry.title: Nvidia research shows robots that train themselves through AI coding agents
entry.summary: Nvidia, CMU, and Berkeley researchers used AI coding agents to teach a fleet of eight robots dexterous grasping in the real world, reaching up to 99 percent success on difficult tasks. The work demonstrates robots that effectively train themselves via agentic code.

entry.title: Will it take a ‘Chernobyl-scale disaster’ for us to regulate AI? | Stuart Russell
entry.summary: Stuart Russell argues regulation may only follow a catastrophic AI failure, pointing to Anthropic's reported early signs of recursive self-improvement and dual-use cyber capabilities. The column frames the Fable/Mythos episode and RSI claims as more consequential than Anthropic's IPO plans.

entry.title: A near-autonomous AI chemist improves a challenging reaction in medicinal chemistry
entry.summary: OpenAI and Molecule.one demonstrated a near-autonomous AI chemist using GPT-5.4 that improved a challenging medicinal-chemistry reaction. The work advances AI's role in real drug-making research.

entry.title: [AINews] GLM-5.2: the top Frontend Coding model in the world, IndexShare for Speculative Decoding
entry.summary: Latent.Space's AINews highlights GLM-5.2 as a top frontend coding model, reportedly just behind Claude Opus 4.8 despite roughly 744B parameters, plus IndexShare for speculative decoding. It frames GLM-5.2 as a strong default coding model released opportunistically after the Fable ban.

entry.title: "Dangerous" AI models are coming no matter what
entry.summary: Anthropic pulled Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 offline after a US export-control directive barring foreign nationals from using them, and remains in unresolved talks with the White House. The piece highlights the dual-use nature of Mythos's vulnerability-finding capabilities, which can aid both defenders and attackers.

entry.title: Anthropic got hit by export rules nobody understands
entry.summary: The Verge reports the Trump administration abruptly ordered Anthropic to cut access for all foreign nationals, forcing it to block Fable 5 and Mythos 5 even for US users and its own employees. Experts note this is the first known use of US export controls to restrict access to an AI model in this manner.

entry.title: AI coding agents taught robots how to install GPUs and cut zip ties
entry.summary: Nvidia's GEAR lab, with CMU and Berkeley collaborators, built an agent harness called ENPIRE that lets AI coding agents autonomously design training regimens for robotic arms. The agents taught a fleet of robots dexterous tasks like cutting zip ties and inserting GPUs into motherboard sockets, reportedly reaching near-99 percent success on tricky manipulation.

entry.title: The Korean Telecom Giant at the Center of Anthropic’s Mythos Controversy
entry.summary: WIRED reports the White House ordered Anthropic to revoke SK Telecom's access to Claude Mythos days before the broader shutdown, citing alleged ties to China. The piece adds national-security and geopolitical detail to the Anthropic export-control crisis.

entry.title: Hyperscalers may soon be unable to fund their AI buildout from cash flow alone
entry.summary: Epoch AI analysis finds Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Oracle are growing AI infrastructure spending about 70 percent annually while operating cash flow rises only 23 percent. Spending could exceed cash flow as early as Q3 2026, pushing firms toward outside funding.

entry.title: MiniMax Sparse Attention (MSA): a Two-Branch Block-Sparse Attention Trained on a 109B-Parameter MoE With a 3T-Token Budget
entry.summary: MiniMax released MSA, a two-branch block-sparse attention method built on grouped-query attention to cut the quadratic cost of long-context softmax attention. It was tested in a 109B-parameter MoE, open-sourced as an inference kernel, and shipped in the production model MiniMax-M3.

entry.title: OpenAI’s Deployment Simulation Extends Pre-Deployment Risk Assessment to Agentic Coding Through Simulated Tool Calls
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, OpenAI published a pre-deployment safety method called Deployment Simulation that replays past conversations through a candidate model to study behavior before launch, extended to agentic coding via simulated tool calls. The privacy-preserving technique has already informed mitigations and surfaced evaluation blind spots.

entry.title: OpenAI researchers want to predict how often AI models will fail before launch
entry.summary: OpenAI researchers proposed a method to predict how frequently a new model will make mistakes after release, aiming to fill gaps left by standard safety testing. The approach targets better pre-launch failure-rate estimation.

entry.title: New research shows how AMIE, our medical AI, could help manage health conditions.
entry.summary: Google DeepMind published Nature research showing its medical AI AMIE could help manage ongoing health conditions, extending beyond diagnosis to disease management. The peer-reviewed work strengthens evidence for clinical AI assistance.

entry.title: Vibe-decoding the White House-Anthropic fight over Fable
entry.summary: A Verge column dissects the factional politics inside the White House-Anthropic fight over Fable, photographed against the G7 summit. It argues the dispute could reshape frontier AI development and US-industry relations.

entry.title: Collecting robot training data is dirty, unglamorous work. Some AI labs are already paying XDOF to do it.
entry.summary: TechCrunch profiles XDOF, a startup paid by AI labs to collect the unglamorous physical-world data needed to train robots. It frames robot training data as a critical bottleneck for physical AI to match LLM progress.

entry.title: The next humanoid robot might not look human at all
entry.summary: French startup Genesis AI, backed by Eric Schmidt, unveiled Eno, a general-purpose robot that abandons human form, sitting on a wheeled folding base while keeping human-matched hands. The design argues humanoid robots need not look human.

entry.title: Vercel Releases Eve: An Open-Source AI Agent Framework Where Each Agent is a Directory of Files Mapped to Capabilities
entry.summary: Vercel open-sourced eve, an Apache-2.0 framework where each agent is a directory of files mapped to capabilities, designed for durable backend agents. Vercel says it already runs more than a hundred agents in production on the framework.

entry.title: Introducing LifeSciBench
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced LifeSciBench, an expert-authored and expert-reviewed benchmark for evaluating how AI systems handle real-world life-science research tasks and decisions. It targets rigorous assessment of AI in scientific workflows.

entry.title: Only 16 percent of Americans think AI will have a positive impact on society, a new study shows
entry.summary: A new Pew Research report finds only 16 percent of Americans believe AI will positively impact society, contrasting sharply with Wall Street enthusiasm. The study underscores a widening gap between investor optimism and public sentiment.

entry.title: Two-thirds of Americans think AI is advancing too quickly
entry.summary: A Pew poll finds 49 percent of Americans now use chatbots at least occasionally, up from 33 percent in 2024, yet 63 percent believe the technology is advancing too quickly. Younger users adopt AI more but hold more pessimistic views.

entry.title: Microsoft researcher builds a working neural network out of goats in Age of Empires II to critique AI science
entry.summary: A Microsoft researcher built a functioning neural network out of goats, bridges, and ice ramps in the Age of Empires II map editor to critique AI science. His review of 315 papers found over half assume language models have human-like traits before experiments begin.

entry.title: Pramaana Labs raises $27M seed round from Khosla Ventures to bring formal verification to AI
entry.summary: Pramaana Labs raised a $27M seed from Khosla Ventures to bring formal verification to AI in high-stakes verticals like law, drug discovery, and tax prep. The aim is provable reliability where errors are costly.

entry.title: How Musicians Can Get Paid for Training AI
entry.summary: IEEE Spectrum reports on companies like Sureel and SoundVerse building attribution systems so musicians can be paid when their work informs AI model outputs. The effort aims to restore the use-equals-payment principle disrupted by generative AI training.

entry.title: NEA’s Tiffany Luck says enterprises are still figuring out their AI ROI
entry.summary: NEA's Tiffany Luck argues enterprises are still struggling to quantify AI ROI after a token-spending spree, citing Uber blowing through its AI budget and companies cutting Claude licenses. The video frames a backlash against unchecked AI usage.

entry.title: Canadian pension giant joins race to fund India’s AI-fueled data center boom
entry.summary: Canada Pension Plan Investment Board is acquiring an 8.2 percent stake in Indian data-center operator CtrlS, joining the rush to fund India's AI infrastructure boom. The deal reflects growing institutional capital flowing into AI compute capacity.

entry.title: 🔬 The Self-Driving Lab — Joseph Krause, Radical AI
entry.summary: A Latent.Space podcast features Radical AI on self-driving labs for materials science, discussing why materials are harder to model than biology due to macro variables like supply chains, microstructures, and manufacturing. The episode references LK99 reproducibility issues as illustrative.

entry.title: The curious case of Elias Thorne – and what he tells us about AI inbreeding | Arwa Mahdawi
entry.summary: An opinion column examines the recurring appearance of a fictional character named Elias Thorne across many LLM-generated stories, including ChatGPT and Claude outputs. The phenomenon is framed as a possible warning sign of model collapse from AI training on AI-generated content.

entry.title: NEA’s Tiffany Luck on AI IPOs, personal agents, and the ROI reckoning
entry.summary: An NEA podcast with Tiffany Luck covers AI IPOs, personal agents, and the enterprise ROI reckoning following the token-spending craze. It revisits the cooling of unchecked AI budgets across major firms.

entry.title: AI search grounded in Facebook posts? What could go wrong?
entry.summary: Meta is adding an AI Mode to Facebook search that answers complex queries using public posts from Facebook Groups and Instagram Reels. The hands-on notes it remains error-prone, raising reliability concerns about grounding answers in social posts.

entry.title: AWS’s New Agentic Tools Trail Rivals, but Respond to Real Problems
entry.summary: AI Business reviews AWS's latest agentic AI tools, concluding they respond to genuine customer problems but trail rivals in novelty. The coverage frames AWS as a fast follower rather than an innovator in agentic AI.

entry.title: Getting more from each token: How Copilot improves context handling and model routing
entry.summary: GitHub described how Copilot improves token efficiency by reducing repeated context, tool definitions, and cached state across longer agentic sessions, while expanding its Auto model-routing to pick the right model per task. The focus is doing more useful work per token.

entry.title: Anthropic becomes first AI startup to join the Frontier carbon removal coalition
entry.summary: Anthropic became the first AI startup to join the Frontier carbon-removal coalition, which secured another $915M in pledges. The move ties AI compute growth to carbon-removal commitments.

entry.title: Google bets on Gemini to reinvent the smart home speaker
entry.summary: Google's $99.99 Gemini-powered Home Speaker swaps rigid Assistant commands for conversational interactions, betting generative AI can revive the smart-speaker category. The launch marks Google's first new audio device in years.

entry.title: Context intelligence for your data and AI agents at scale
entry.summary: At AWS Summit NYC, Amazon previewed AWS Context, a forthcoming service that automatically maps relationships across enterprise data into a knowledge layer for AI agents. The goal is to give agents trusted, governed context for decision-making.

entry.title: Ten months later, the $100 Google Home Speaker is finally available for preorder
entry.summary: Google opened preorders for its $100 Gemini-powered Home Speaker, its first smart speaker in roughly six years, shipping June 25. The device replaces rigid assistant commands with conversational Gemini interactions.

entry.title: The Gemini-Powered Google Home Speaker Is Finally Here
entry.summary: WIRED details the redesigned Gemini-powered Google Home Speaker, arriving six years after Google's last smart speaker. It is built to host Gemini's chatbot in a HomePod-style form factor.

entry.title: Google’s first smart speaker in six years arrives next week
entry.summary: Google's $99 Home Speaker, built for Gemini for Home, ships June 25 with preorders opening now, narrowly missing its promised spring window. Hardware is unchanged from the announcement nine months ago.

entry.title: New in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Build agents with broader knowledge and continuous learning
entry.summary: AWS updated Amazon Bedrock AgentCore with features for broader knowledge access and continuous learning, aiming to close the context-and-feedback gap that limits agent performance. The update connects agents to more enterprise data sources and adds systematic feedback.

entry.title: I had a blood clot. An AI diagnosis may have saved my life | Gleb Tsipursky
entry.summary: A columnist recounts how an AI tool flagged a possible blood clot that a chiropractor missed, arguing AI and physicians together could be beneficial while stressing regulation. The piece is a personal opinion on AI's role in diagnosis.

entry.title: Pinterest launches an experimental AI shopping app called ‘Ask Pinterest’
entry.summary: Pinterest launched an experimental AI shopping app called Ask Pinterest that delivers recommendations and inspiration through a conversational interface. The app extends Pinterest's discovery model into agentic commerce.

entry.title: Get back hours every day with autonomous agents in Amazon Quick
entry.summary: AWS expanded Amazon Quick with autonomous background agents, an activity feed for prioritization, and cross-data-source insights. The assistant aims to complete busywork like deal follow-ups and meeting prep while users focus elsewhere.

entry.title: From the Hugging Face Hub to robot hardware with Strands Agents and LeRobot
entry.summary: A Hugging Face blog post walks through going from the Hugging Face Hub to physical robot hardware using Strands Agents and LeRobot. It connects model and agent tooling to embodied deployment.

entry.title: How to Build Memory-Efficient Transformers with xFormers Using Packed Sequences, GQA, ALiBi, SwiGLU, and Causal Attention
entry.summary: A MarkTechPost tutorial walks through building memory-efficient Transformers with xFormers using packed sequences, grouped-query attention, ALiBi, SwiGLU, and causal attention. It benchmarks memory-efficient attention against standard attention before assembling a trainable GPT-style model.

entry.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Async Inference now supports inline request payloads
entry.summary: AWS added inline request-payload support to SageMaker Async Inference, letting customers send payloads up to 128,000 bytes directly in the API request instead of uploading to S3. This removes a network round-trip and simplifies async inference workflows.

entry.title: DeepSeek takes outside money for the first time at a $50 billion valuation
entry.summary: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek raised over 50 billion yuan (about 7.4 billion dollars) in its first-ever external funding round at a roughly 50 billion dollar valuation. It marks a major capital influx for a leading open-weight model developer that had previously stayed self-funded.

entry.title: Leaked financial docs show OpenAI is losing billions of dollars a year
entry.summary: Leaked audited financials show OpenAI revenue grew from 3.7 billion dollars in 2024 to 13.07 billion in 2025, approaching nearly 2 billion in monthly revenue by year-end, but expenses (especially R&D) far outpace income as it preps for an IPO. The documents reveal multi-billion-dollar annual losses.

entry.title: SpaceX Aims at Agentic Coding With $60B Cursor Acquisition
entry.summary: AI Business covers SpaceX's 60 billion dollar Cursor acquisition as a push into agentic coding, gaining access to Cursor's developer workflow and user analytics. It frames the deal as expanding SpaceX's developer offerings.

entry.title: Meet Qwen-RobotSuite: Three Embodied AI Models for VLA Manipulation, Video World Modeling, and Navigation
entry.summary: Qwen released Qwen-Robot-Suite, three embodied-AI foundation models built on its vision-language backbones: RobotManip (VLA manipulation on Qwen3.5-4B), RobotWorld (a language-conditioned video world model), and RobotNav (navigation at 2B/4B/8B), with two shipping public GitHub repos. It targets fragmented robotics data with a unified open suite.

entry.title: Critical Copilot vulnerability allowed hackers to steal 2FA code from users
entry.summary: Microsoft patched a max-critical M365 Copilot flaw that researchers showed could exfiltrate 2FA codes and other sensitive email data via prompt injection. The case underscores the unsolved problem of LLMs failing to separate trusted user instructions from malicious third-party content.

entry.title: Predicting model behavior before release by simulating deployment
entry.summary: OpenAI introduced Deployment Simulation, a method that predicts AI model behavior before release by simulating deployment using real conversation data to improve safety and evaluation accuracy. It aims to catch behavioral issues pre-launch.

entry.title: OpenAI burned through $34 billion last year
entry.summary: The Decoder reports OpenAI spent 34 billion dollars over the past year, far more than the prior year, underscoring the enormous cash burn behind its growth ahead of a potential IPO. It complements leaked financials showing expenses outpacing revenue.

entry.title: Trump admin tries to block Clean Air Act lawsuit over xAI's gas turbines
entry.summary: The Trump administration filed in support of xAI against an NAACP Clean Air Act suit over 57-plus unpermitted gas turbines powering the Colossus 2 data center in Mississippi, arguing the facility runs Grok systems the military needs. The case ties AI data-center buildout directly to environmental and national-security politics.

entry.title: SpaceX to acquire AI coding platform Cursor for $60 billion
entry.summary: SpaceX agreed to acquire AI coding tool Cursor for 60 billion dollars in an all-stock deal expected to close in Q3, days after its IPO and months after merging with xAI. The move aims to bolster the combined company's coding offering against Anthropic and OpenAI.

entry.title: SpaceX to acquire Cursor for $60B in stock, days after blockbuster IPO
entry.summary: SpaceX will acquire Cursor for 60 billion dollars in stock days after its blockbuster IPO, aiming to revive its struggling AI division which it touts as targeting a 26 trillion dollar AI market. The deal stems from an earlier acquire-or-pay arrangement.

entry.title: SpaceX is officially buying Cursor for $60 billion
entry.summary: The Verge confirms SpaceX is officially buying Cursor for 60 billion dollars, a bet to win enterprise customers and close the gap with Anthropic and OpenAI, stemming from an April acquire-or-pay-10-billion arrangement. The deal is expected to close in Q3.

entry.title: SpaceX bets $60 billion on Cursor to catch OpenAI and Anthropic
entry.summary: The Decoder reports SpaceX is buying Cursor-maker Anysphere for 60 billion dollars just two trading days after its IPO to help the struggling xAI division catch Anthropic and OpenAI. It frames the deal as a catch-up play in agentic coding.

entry.title: Inside the fight over Claude Mythos 5
entry.summary: The Verge details Anthropic's weekend scramble after a Friday US export-control directive ordered it to block any foreign national from accessing Mythos 5 and Fable 5, forcing it to disable the products entirely and lobby Trump in person. It exposes the operational chaos of capability-based export controls.

entry.title: Anthropic Is Still at Odds With the White House Over Claude Fable 5

author.name: Hugo Lowell, Lily Hay Newman, Maxwell Zeff

entry.summary: Anthropic leaders met White House officials in Washington but remained split over the risk posed by Claude Fable 5 after the government's export-control directive. The standoff highlights tension between a frontier lab and the administration over dangerous-capability models.

entry.title: ‘Dangerous’ AI Models Are Coming No Matter What
entry.summary: Wired argues the US crackdown on Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 obscures the reality that AI models with advanced offensive hacking capabilities will inevitably proliferate. It frames export controls on a single model as insufficient against a broad capability trend.

entry.title: France to ditch Palantir’s AI data tools in favour of domestic provider
entry.summary: France's domestic intelligence service will drop Palantir's AI data tools for French provider ChapsVision, with the PM citing the need to avoid strategic dependence on foreign-controlled tools. It is a concrete sovereignty-driven procurement shift.

entry.title: ChatGPT’s market share slips below 50% for first time
entry.summary: ChatGPT's global market share dipped below 50 percent for the first time, though it remains the leader with over 1.1 billion monthly users, ahead of Gemini at 662 million and Claude at 245 million. The data signals intensifying competition among assistants.

entry.title: Microsoft's Copilot Cowork moves to usage-based billing and may tap DeepSeek
entry.summary: Microsoft is moving Copilot Cowork to usage-based billing because flat-rate pricing is unsustainable and is reportedly evaluating a fine-tuned DeepSeek V4 as a cheaper backend option. The moves reflect industry-wide cost pressures in agentic AI.

entry.title: Berlin court rules Google's AI Overviews are just a new search format, not original content
entry.summary: A Berlin court ruled Google's AI Overviews are merely a new search-result format over which Google has no decisive content influence, partly contradicting a recent Munich ruling that held Google liable for false AI answers. The split underscores unsettled legal liability for AI-generated summaries.

entry.title: Google Cloud Introduces Open Knowledge Format (OKF): A Vendor-Neutral Markdown Spec for Giving AI Agents Curated Context
entry.summary: Google Cloud introduced the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), a vendor-neutral markdown-plus-YAML spec for giving AI agents curated, portable context like schemas, metric definitions, and runbooks. The v0.1 format aims to standardize the LLM-wiki pattern across tools.

entry.title: Pentagon boasts of using AI to write reports mandated by Congress
entry.summary: The Pentagon publicly touted using generative AI, starting with Google Cloud Gemini for Government, to draft hundreds of congressionally mandated national-security reports. It signals deep institutional adoption of LLMs in sensitive government workflows.

entry.title: DOJ Lawyers Argue xAI Is ‘Vital’ for National Security in NAACP Lawsuit
entry.summary: The DOJ argued in court that xAI is vital to national security, including operations in the Iran War, to dismiss the NAACP pollution suit over its gas turbines. It is another framing of the government defending Musk's AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Unlocking UK house-building with AI-accelerated planning
entry.summary: The UK government partnered with Google DeepMind to build an AI-powered prototype aimed at speeding up housing planning decisions. It represents applied AI for public-sector administrative bottlenecks.

entry.title: Trump’s DoJ intervenes to back Elon Musk in datacenter pollution lawsuit
entry.summary: The Guardian reports the DOJ urged a federal court to dismiss the NAACP suit over xAI's unpermitted methane-gas turbines in Mississippi, defending Musk's data center on national-security grounds. The turbines allegedly emit toxic pollutants without air permits.

entry.title: The Anthropic ‘Fable’ saga proves: we have opened the AI Pandora’s box. What now? | Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier
entry.summary: An op-ed by Sanders and Schneier argues the government's classification of Anthropic's Fable model as a dangerous munition and resulting access shutdown won't help, because the real issue is the general rise in AI capabilities. They call for collective action that is currently politically unattainable.

entry.title: Android 17 launches with new multitasking tools as Google expands Gemini features
entry.summary: Google released Android 17 and Wear OS 7 with new multitasking, parental controls, and security tools, alongside a Pixel Drop bringing its latest AI models to devices. The update broadens Gemini feature distribution across the Android ecosystem.

entry.title: Want to get a data center online quickly? Give it some flex.
entry.summary: MIT Technology Review explains how AI-driven demand-flexibility lets data centers throttle chip power on command—as during a UK grid spike—to ease grid stress and speed up bringing facilities online. It frames flexible load as a key enabler of AI infrastructure expansion.

entry.title: How easily can Russian propaganda fool AI models? A new benchmark finds out
entry.summary: The Institute of the Estonian Language released a benchmark measuring how susceptible AI language models are to Russian propaganda. It offers a concrete tool for evaluating model vulnerability to state disinformation.

entry.title: DOJ claims xAI’s unpermitted gas turbines are a matter of ‘national, economic, and energy security’
entry.summary: TechCrunch covers the DOJ's claim that xAI's unpermitted gas turbines are a matter of national, economic, and energy security, asserting the Pentagon needs them. It is part of the federal effort to keep the turbines running despite the lawsuit.

entry.title: DOJ invokes national security to defend xAI's unpermitted gas turbines in NAACP lawsuit
entry.summary: The Decoder reports the DOJ is invoking national security—calling Grok essential to military operations—to defend xAI's unpermitted gas turbines in the NAACP suit. It echoes the broader federal defense of Musk's AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Anthropic "pauses" token-based billing for its Claude Agent SDK
entry.summary: Anthropic abruptly paused a planned billing change that would have charged Claude Agent SDK and third-party app usage at API rates rather than from subscription limits, just as it was to take effect. The reversal preserves cheaper access for heavy agentic users amid an emerging price war.

entry.title: Parallelize speculative decoding with P-EAGLE on Amazon SageMaker AI
entry.summary: AWS detailed P-EAGLE on SageMaker, a parallelized speculative-decoding approach that breaks the autoregressive bottleneck in draft-token generation to boost LLM inference throughput. It targets higher production throughput with lower latency.

entry.title: [AINews] Satya on Loopcraft: Building Frontier Ecosystems
entry.summary: A Latent.Space piece recaps Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella's viral framing of competing on frontier ecosystems and learning loops (Loopcraft) over chasing the best model, positioning cognitive loops between people and digital systems as the new corporate IP. It articulates a strategic theory of AI value capture.

entry.title: How the fight over US datacenters is scrambling this state’s politics: ‘We don’t want it’
entry.summary: A report examines how AI data-center expansion is upending Pennsylvania politics, with Governor Shapiro clashing with state lawmakers and residents over the facilities powering the AI boom. Local opposition centers on power, land, and community impact.

entry.title: Anthropic’s latest feud with the Trump admin may actually help it, sales data suggests
entry.summary: TechCrunch reports that Ramp spending data suggests Anthropic's enterprise popularity is rising fast enough that its clash with the Trump administration over Fable 5 and Mythos may actually boost adoption. Business demand appears resilient to the political fight.

entry.title: Anthropic backs off unpopular billing overhaul as price war with OpenAI looms
entry.summary: The Decoder reports Anthropic pulled its planned Claude Agent SDK billing change just before launch, keeping SDK and third-party usage on regular subscription limits amid a looming price war with OpenAI. The reversal favors heavy agentic developers.

entry.title: ABB Robotics Enters Partnership to Advance Physical AI
entry.summary: ABB Robotics partnered with Psyonic to improve robot training systems and advance physical-AI deployment. The collaboration targets better embodied-AI training pipelines.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Adds Asynchronous Subagents, So Delegated Work No Longer Blocks the Parent Chat
entry.summary: Nous Research updated its open-source Hermes Agent so its delegate tool can run subagents asynchronously, meaning delegated work no longer blocks the parent chat. Users enable it via a simple update command.

entry.title: Safeguard your agentic AI applications with the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails InvokeGuardrailChecks API
entry.summary: AWS announced the Amazon Bedrock Guardrails InvokeGuardrailChecks API, letting developers apply individual safety checks at any point in agentic loops without creating guardrail resources, returning numeric scores for custom block/bypass/retry/log actions. It adds finer-grained safety control for agentic apps.

entry.title: Malaysia’s AI agent-powered messaging app Respond.io raises $62.5M, eyes acquisitions
entry.summary: Malaysia's Respond.io raised 62.5 million dollars for its AI-agent customer-messaging platform that charges per conversation rather than per seat and is eyeing acquisitions in North America and Europe. It highlights agentic AI commercialization in Southeast Asia.

entry.title: ‘Pretty Crazy’ Token Usage Is Testing Bosses’ Bet on AI
entry.summary: Wired profiles two companies grappling with surging Claude token consumption, illustrating the emerging challenge of tokenomics as AI compute costs strain business models. It highlights unpredictable spend as agentic usage scales.

entry.title: The new Siri makes one of Apple's most convenient OS features a cumbersome mess
entry.summary: A hands-on review finds Apple's revamped AI-powered Siri, unveiled at WWDC, largely layers Google-style AI Overviews onto existing OS features while making the ecosystem more cumbersome, despite gaining conversational ability. The verdict is skeptical of the hype.

entry.title: Plaud says its software business topped $100M in ARR after shipping over 2M AI notetakers
entry.summary: AI notetaker maker Plaud says its software business crossed 100 million dollars in ARR after shipping over 2 million devices. It marks a notable scale milestone in the crowded AI meeting-assistant hardware market.

entry.title: Probably raises $9M to build a more reliable kind of AI
entry.summary: Startup Probably raised 9 million dollars, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, to build AI that avoids hallucinations and factual errors with accuracy closer to deterministic systems. It targets reliability as a core product differentiator.

entry.title: Timnit Gebru on how to safeguard independent science for the AI age | Scientific American
entry.summary: Scientific American profiles Timnit Gebru and her Distributed AI Research Institute, focusing on safeguarding independent, community-rooted AI research amid big-tech dominance. It spotlights independence and inclusion in AI science.

entry.title: EMEA Firms Lack AI Visibility Despite Sovereignty Push, IBM Reports
entry.summary: An IBM report finds many EMEA firms treat AI sovereignty as strategic yet lack visibility into the infrastructure underpinning their AI systems. It highlights a gap between sovereignty ambitions and operational understanding.

entry.title: Introducing container caching in Amazon SageMaker AI for faster model scaling
entry.summary: AWS introduced container image caching for SageMaker AI inference, claiming up to 2x faster end-to-end latency during scale-out for generative AI models. It continues SageMaker's focus on faster model scaling.

entry.title: Meet Atoms: A Vibe Coding Tool That Uses AI Agents to Build, Deploy, and Market Your App (No Code)
entry.summary: A sponsored piece showcases Atoms, a no-code vibe-coding tool that uses AI agents to build, deploy, and market apps, including validation, SEO, ad campaigns, and analytics. It pitches an end-to-end agentic app-building workflow.

entry.title: How to Build a Parsing Pipeline with Docling Parse for Layout-Aware Document Intelligence
entry.summary: A tutorial demonstrates building a layout-aware document-parsing pipeline with Docling Parse to extract words, characters, and lines with page coordinates and export structured JSON/CSV for document-AI tasks. It targets retrieval-ready document preparation.

entry.title: The US government may be asking Anthropic the impossible by demanding unhackable LLMs
