entry.title: Chipmaker Nvidia seeks to raise over $25B in first bond deal since 2021

author.name: Michelle Chan and Tim Bradshaw, Financial Times

entry.summary: Nvidia is launching its first bond sale since 2021, upsizing the offering from $20B to over $25B after attracting more than $85B in orders. The seven-part deal spans two- to 30-year maturities and serves as a test of investor appetite for AI sector exposure.

entry.title: Z.ai Launches GLM-5.2 With a Usable 1M-Token Context, Two Thinking-Effort Levels, and No Benchmarks at Launch
entry.summary: Z.ai launched GLM-5.2, its fourth flagship coding-tier model in roughly four months, featuring a usable 1M-token context window (a 5x jump over GLM-5.1) and two thinking-effort levels. The release notably shipped without published benchmarks.

entry.title: All the news about Anthropic’s new AI fight with the White House
entry.summary: The Verge compiles the escalating conflict between Anthropic and the White House, which on June 12th ordered foreign access blocked to the recently launched Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Reports indicate the order followed findings that Fable 5 could be coaxed into producing cyberattack-relevant information.

entry.title: Trump’s Anthropic shutdown just made the case for non-American AI
entry.summary: The Verge analyzes how the forced Anthropic shutdown, which blocked all foreign nationals including its own employees, demonstrated US government control over frontier AI access. The episode is framed as strengthening the case for non-American sovereign AI alternatives.

entry.title: The US government’s Anthropic models ban was never about an AI jailbreak
entry.summary: TechCrunch analysis argues the Trump administration's order forcing Anthropic to pull its cybersecurity-capable models was driven by political or retaliatory motives rather than a genuine jailbreak concern. It frames the action as a sign the AI industry faces increasing government interference.

entry.title: Cybersecurity vets protest ‘dangerous’ US government ban on Anthropic’s most powerful models
entry.summary: Dozens of cybersecurity experts petitioned the White House to lift export-control restrictions on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, arguing the ban harms defenders' ability to secure software. The protest underscores tension over dual-use AI capabilities.

entry.title: Anthropic shutdown sparks sovereignty debate across Europe
entry.summary: The European Commission is assessing fallout from the US order that forced Anthropic to shut down Fable 5 and Mythos 5 worldwide, fueling debate over building homegrown foundation models versus securing contractual access. Experts warn Europe lacks the compute, energy, and competitive providers needed for true independence.

entry.title: Sakana AI Commercializes AB-MCTS in Sakana Marlin, an Enterprise Agent Generating Up to 100-Page Research Reports With Slides
entry.summary: Sakana AI shipped its first commercial product, Sakana Marlin, an autonomous B2B research agent positioned as a Virtual Chief Strategy Officer. It runs autonomously for up to eight hours, issuing thousands of LLM queries to produce long reports and slide decks.

entry.title: AI use by the US government is ballooning. And the lack of transparency is troubling | Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier

author.name: Nathan E Sanders and Bruce Schneier

entry.summary: An OMB disclosure reveals 3,611 active or planned federal AI use cases, a 70% jump since the Biden era, including automation of sensitive governmental functions. The opinion piece warns about transparency gaps and the transfer of consequential decisions from humans to machines.

entry.title: Salesforce acquires AI customer service platform Fin for $3.6B
entry.summary: Salesforce is acquiring AI customer service platform Fin for $3.6B to bolster its Agentforce enterprise agent platform. The deal targets improving custom AI agents that automate business tasks.

entry.title: Big Tech’s desperate last push at AI regulation
entry.summary: Big Tech lobbyists are making a final push for federal AI preemption legislation to override the patchwork of state rules, but face roadblocks and political blowback. A potential Democratic House after midterms could end the effort.

entry.title: Meet Flash-KMeans: An IO-Aware, Exact K-Means That Runs Over 200× Faster Than FAISS on GPUs
entry.summary: Researchers from UC Berkeley and UT Austin released Flash-KMeans, an open-source IO-aware exact k-means that reportedly runs up to 200x faster than FAISS and 33x faster than cuML on GPUs. It restructures data movement without approximating, targeting in-loop use during training and inference.

entry.title: Nvidia joins AI debt boom with $20 billion bond sale
entry.summary: The Decoder covers Nvidia's plan to raise at least $20B in its first bond sale since 2021, situating it within a broader AI-driven corporate debt boom. The report cites sources with direct knowledge of the deal.

entry.title: Sarvam becomes India’s newest AI unicorn with $234 million funding round led by HCLTech
entry.summary: Indian startup Sarvam raised $234M led by HCLTech, which invested $150M, reaching unicorn status. The Bengaluru company strengthens India's domestic AI ecosystem.

entry.title: Pokémon Go data helped train AI now linked to military drones
entry.summary: The Decoder reports that volunteer AR scans from Pokémon Go players, used to train Niantic's spatial AI, are now being combined with a US defense contractor's software for GPS-free navigation. The story highlights how consumer-sourced data feeds into military drone applications.

entry.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warns of "a small number of AI systems capturing all the economic returns"
entry.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella warned that a small number of AI systems could capture all economic returns and urged companies to build proprietary token capital from internal data. The framing also aligns with Microsoft's Azure business interests.

entry.title: As AI agents become employees, NewCore emerges with $66M to give them identities
entry.summary: NewCore launched with $66M to provide identity and security management for AI agents acting as enterprise workers. The startup argues managing agent identities will become the next major enterprise security challenge.

entry.title: Cohere North Mini Code Gives AI Developers More Control
entry.summary: Cohere released North Mini Code, targeting developers who find frontier models from Anthropic and OpenAI too opaque or heavyweight for their tasks. The product emphasizes transparency and control.

entry.title: The AI layoff wave is becoming a powder keg
entry.summary: TechCrunch examines mounting tension as AI-driven layoffs hit tens of thousands of workers while a small group of AI insiders amasses extreme wealth. The piece frames the growing inequality as a potential flashpoint.

entry.title: Schneider Electric, Foxconn Partner to Build Next-Gen Data Centers
entry.summary: Schneider Electric and Foxconn partnered to build next-generation data centers using scalable, replicable design blueprints. The deal aims to ease AI infrastructure bottlenecks.

entry.title: Meta’s new ‘AI Mode’ on Facebook pulls from public info across its platforms
entry.summary: Meta is rolling out an AI Mode on Facebook that generates results pulling from public posts across its platforms, alongside other AI features. The move reflects Meta's effort to boost engagement and catch up in the AI race.

entry.title: Andrew Hastie compares AI to cold-war nuclear arms race and warns Australia may fall behind
entry.summary: Australian Liberal MP Andrew Hastie compared AI development to the cold-war nuclear arms race and urged major national investment to preserve strategic independence from AI superpowers. He proposed positioning Australia as a southern hemisphere technology hub.

entry.title: Introducing Gemma 4 models on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: AWS announced availability of Google DeepMind's Gemma 4 open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock, including three instruction-tuned variants with reasoning, function calling, and multimodal input. Gemma 4 launched in April 2026, so this is a platform availability update.

entry.title: AI Agent Failure Detection and Root Cause Analysis with Strands Evals
entry.summary: AWS detailed Strands Evals SDK detectors that automatically identify AI agent failures and perform root cause analysis on execution traces. The tooling aims to cut diagnosis time for production agents from hours to minutes.

entry.title: Facebook’s new AI Mode search gets its info from public posts
entry.summary: The Verge details Meta's new Facebook AI Mode search, which draws on public posts across Meta platforms to generate results instead of just links. It accompanies other features like photo presets and collage templates.

entry.title: Anthropic Forced to Disable New Models by US Government
entry.summary: As first reported in our News coverage yesterday, AI Business reports that the US government forced Anthropic to disable two powerful new models shortly after their release, marking the latest clash with the Trump administration. The piece situates it in the ongoing vendor-government tension.

entry.title: Sundar Pichai faces boos, walkout at Stanford graduation ceremony over Google’s Israel, ICE ties
entry.summary: Sundar Pichai faced boos and a walkout at Stanford's graduation over Google's defense ties to Israel and ICE. The protest centered on AI's role in Google's defense contracts.

entry.title: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth Admits the Company’s AI Reorg Was ‘Atrocious’
entry.summary: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth admitted in an internal memo that the company's AI reorganization was handled poorly, promising employees more stability and restored perks. The note reflects ongoing internal turmoil amid Meta's aggressive AI push.

entry.title: Build context-rich research agents with Deep Agents and Bedrock AgentCore
entry.summary: AWS published a guide on building research agents using LangChain Deep Agents and Bedrock AgentCore, delegating deep work to isolated subagents that return concise results. It addresses context-window limits in multi-step research workflows.

entry.title: Why do South Koreans love AI so much?
entry.summary: An MIT Technology Review feature explores South Korea's enthusiastic embrace of AI and automation, from facial-recognition immigration to delivery robots. It examines cultural and infrastructural factors behind the country's adoption.

entry.title: Claude Code Guide 2026: 25 Features with Examples + Demo
entry.summary: MarkTechPost published a guide covering 25 features and strategies for Claude Code, Anthropic's agentic coding tool that now layers memory, hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, and MCP. The piece is a practical reference for engineers scaling the tool.

entry.title: GitHub Copilot CLI for Beginners: Overview of common slash commands
entry.summary: A GitHub blog beginner tutorial explains slash commands in GitHub Copilot CLI, covering tasks like switching models, checking token usage, and resuming sessions from the terminal. It is part of an ongoing educational series.

entry.title: Databricks Open-Sources Omnigent: A Meta-Harness That Composes, Governs, and Shares AI Agents Across Claude Code, Codex, and Pi
entry.summary: Databricks open-sourced Omnigent under Apache 2.0, a meta-harness that sits above individual agent harnesses like Claude Code, Codex, and Pi to enable composition, governance, and sharing across them. It addresses the fragmentation engineers face when juggling multiple coding and search agents.

entry.title: China may have accessed Mythos
entry.summary: A Semafor report cited by The Verge says the White House's export restrictions on Anthropic's Mythos were partly driven by fears that a China-linked group had accessed the model, raising distillation and reverse-engineering risks. The administration has not confirmed the China angle, and a Trump advisor's public statement emphasized other concerns.

entry.title: Amazon and five other companies reportedly triggered the government crackdown on Anthropic's Fable model
entry.summary: Reporting indicates Amazon CEO Andy Jassy and executives from five other companies warned the Trump administration about security vulnerabilities in Anthropic's Fable model, prompting a rapid White House export-control order that forced the model offline. Notably, Amazon is one of Anthropic's largest investors, raising questions about competitive motives behind the security framing.

entry.title: As Anthropic suspends access to new models, India debates its AI future
entry.summary: First spotted on Reddit, now mainstream coverage explores India's sovereign AI debate, Following the suspension of access to Anthropic's newest models, Indian tech leaders are debating whether dependence on foreign frontier labs is a wake-up call for building sovereign AI capacity. The article ties the Anthropic export-control episode to broader questions about India's AI strategy.

entry.title: AI coding agents find the right file but miss the exact lines that matter, study shows
entry.summary: A new benchmark called SWE-Explore separates code search from code repair and finds that leading coding agents reliably locate the correct file but miss most of the critical lines within it. The study suggests insufficient context retrieval undermines fixes even when models are otherwise capable.

entry.title: Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
entry.summary: OpenAI launched a Partner Network backed by a $150M investment to help global partners accelerate enterprise AI deployment and transformation. The program targets scaling adoption through a structured ecosystem of integrators and consultants.

entry.title: Google Cloud's Open Knowledge Format turns scattered docs into Markdown files for AI agents
entry.summary: Google Cloud introduced the Open Knowledge Format (OKF), a minimalist spec that standardizes scattered organizational documents into Markdown with YAML frontmatter so AI agents can consume them. It formalizes the LLM Wiki pattern recently popularized by Andrej Karpathy.

entry.title: KPMG fabricated AI case studies in a report designed to sell clients on AI adoption
entry.summary: KPMG pulled a report promoting AI adoption after it was found to contain fabricated case studies involving organizations like UBS and the NHS. The episode highlights what GPTZero's CEO calls secondary hallucinations, where unverified AI-generated claims spread through trusted consulting channels.

entry.title: As AI companies race to go public, who else is along for the ride?
entry.summary: A TechCrunch Equity podcast segment examines the wave of AI companies preparing to go public and which adjacent startups stand to benefit, framing it around momentum from a SpaceX IPO. The piece is commentary on market dynamics rather than a specific deal or filing.

entry.title: A Coding Hands-On on FineWeb for Streaming, Filtering, Deduplication, Tokenization, and Large-Scale Web Corpus Analytics
entry.summary: A hands-on tutorial walks through streaming, filtering, deduplication, and tokenization workflows on the FineWeb web corpus without downloading the full multi-terabyte dataset. It reproduces simplified versions of FineWeb's quality pipeline and MinHash near-duplicate detection.
